https://www.politico.eu/article/jordan-b.text: LUXEMBOURG — The European Parliament has “paranoia” when it comes to the far-right, Jordan Bardella’s lawyer claimed as his client fights to keep his right-hand man on the EU payroll. Bardella took the Parliament to the EU’s General Court over its decision to stop François Paradol from working as a part-time MEP assistant, although the president of France’s far-right National Rally was not present in court on Wednesday. Paradol, Bardella’s chief of staff, used to work as his part-time local MEP assistant in France. But in 2024, the Parliament turned down his reappointment in the wake of a case involving Bardella’s mentor, Marine Le Pen. She was found guilty of embezzling cash meant for MEPs from 2004 to 2016, and using the money to pay for national party staff. Advertisement Advertisement Bardella’s lawyer, David Dassa-Le Deist, told the court the decision was taken because of “prejudice” against far-right parties such as the National Rally. “There is a paranoia within the Parliament about the members who work for the far-right,” Dassa-Le Deist said. Bardella had proposed that Paradol work every Monday to Thursday morning as a parliamentary assistant, with the rest of his time set aside for national party work. The Parliament said no, claiming it would be near-impossible for Paradol to separate his duties. The Parliament’s lawyer, Lavinia Darie, backed up that decision Wednesday, saying Paradol’s National Rally job would mean him being available “around the clock.” She also disputed whether Paradol could decline to perform National Rally tasks for Bardella when he was supposed to be working as an MEP assistant. She added that the case involving Le Pen showed there was a “high risk of abuse of funds” in Bardella’s case. The National Rally is on course to win next year’s French election. If Le Pen becomes president, Bardella could well be her prime minister. Dassa-Le Deist said the rejection was unfair given hybrid working situations are “not prohibited,” adding that the “very competent” Paradol had been working with Bardella “for a very long time” and “knew how to carry out both of these roles.” Judge Heikki Kanninen asked the Parliament’s lawyer whether they would have made the same decision if it involved an MEP from a different party. Advertisement Advertisement “Such a case — for everyone — would have been refused independent of which member, which political group, or which nationality put this request forward,” Darie said. “It’s the duty of the officer to respect the good management of public funds.” The case could have ramifications for MEPs’ ability to choose their own staffers. Paradol told POLITICO last year that by blocking his appointment, the Parliament was attempting to “turn every political aide into a European civil servant.” Judges didn’t confirm when a decision can be expected, but the court usually takes a few months to make a ruling. Victor Goury-Laffont contributed to this article .

Photograph: Yves Herman/Reuters Venice film festival Venice best actress winner says she signed on at Danish job centre days before her victory Mathilde Arcel, who won the Volpi Cup on Saturday for her role in Golden Lion winner Woman Unknown, said job offers have now begun to arrive Philip Oltermann European culture editor Tue 15 Sep 2026 06.37 EDT Last modified on Tue 15 Sep 2026 06.38 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The winner of this year’s best actress prize at the Venice film festival has revealed that she is on unemployment benefits and had to fly to back to Copenhagen to report to the job centre before receiving her award. On Saturday night, Danish actor Mathilde Arcel won the prestigious Volpi Cup for her first leading role in a feature film, May el-Toukhy’s post-second world war drama Woman Unknown, which also won the Golden Lion award for best film. Jury president Maggie Gyllenhaal said the judges had been able to relax Venice rules around not awarding more than one prize per film because the vote for Arcel had been unanimous. Bold and bravura choices as Venice celebrates A Woman Unknown, Possible Love and NAZA Read more After her triumph, the 30-year-old actor revealed in interviews with Danish media that she had returned to Denmark after her film’s premiere to sign on at the job centre, as she is on unemployment benefits when not working on films. She then returned to the Lido after being told it would be wise to be present at the awards gala. In the UK, actors’ trade union Equity said in a 2023 report that 63% of its members have been in receipt of social security at some point in their life. Set in the direct aftermath of the Nazi occupation of Denmark, Woman Unknown tells the story of Marie, a young housemaid and nanny who is about to marry her widowed industrialist employer. But a chance encounter with an old schoolfriend threatens to reveal a shameful secret, exposing Marie to the retributive hounding of female “horizontal collaborators” who had intimate relations with German soldiers. At Venice, Arcel drew wide critical praise for the contained inner anguish she brings to the role of Marie. “Mathilde is going to blow our socks off,” Gyllenhaal said in a press conference after the awards ceremony. The actor said her agent had received several calls with new job offers since she scooped the Volpi Cup, the male version of which went to Hollywood veteran John Malkovich. “There are a lot of calls and a lot of interest from abroad and things like that, and we need to talk about what’s going to happen,” she told Danish broadcaster DR. Speaking in Venice on Saturday night, Arcel joked that her ultimate dream would be to play a part in one long-running British TV detective drama she was particularly fond of. “I really want to keep on working and meet some new artists”, she said. “I’m looking so much forward to what the future will bring, perhaps even a role in Midsomer Murders”.
